info.timeAllocation:
Hours Per Course: 30 sessions

1 session = 90 minutes
info.description:
A- Listening: Upon completion of the course, students should be able to

- Listen to talk shows or radio shows to identify main ideas (U1)

- Listen for rhetorical questions via an invention description (U2)

- Listen to radio news programs or reports to look for bias (U2), reasons and explanations (U3), summaries (U3) , or listen to understand a sequence of events (U4)

- Listen to lectures for similarities and differences (U5), for supporting statements (U5), or listen to know phrases used to introduce examples (U1)

- Listen to a presentation for organization cues to distinguish facts and opinions (U4)

B- Speaking: Upon completion of the course, students should be able to

- Use appropriate language to let other people know that they are paying attention and that they are interested in what people are saying during a conversation or informal discussion (U1)

- Give examples to express ideas clearly and convincingly (U2)

- Give reasons to contribute to an academic discussion (U3)

- Change and return to topics in a conversation (U4)

- Interrupt politely during a lecture or a classroom discussion to understand it clearly (U5)

- Pronounce correctly thought groups (know how to pause correctly) (U1) and weak forms of ‘that’ and ‘as’ (U2)

- Use appropriate language express disagreement politely (U3)

- Know and use intonation patterns in questions and to express feelings and attitudes (U4)

- Stress correctly to express the right meanings and to emphasize important information (U5)

- Introduce themselves (U1)

- Discuss the result of an experiment, research findings and applications, and water issues (U3)

- Present the pros and cons of an invention; about a city, a plan for a public space, future problems and personal and community values. (U2, U5)

- debate an argument.
info.studentTasks:
- Attend more than 80% of in-class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfil tasks given by intructor after class

- Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes

- Use CD-ROM provided with the textbook

- Access the course website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.
